concerns_addressed: Hardcoded hex values (#006B3F, #F5A623, #C4D600, #4ECDC4) in .status-active, .status-ongoing, .status-reschedule, .status-cancel color/border properties replaced with CSS variable references (var(--primary-color), var(--accent-orange), var(--accent-yellow), var(--accent-blue))
Same fix applied to .board-status.status-* color properties (4 additional replacements)
Test expectations in tests/css/style.test.js updated in lockstep to match CSS variable references
Old status badge styles (.status-menunggu, .status-meeting, .status-selesai) confirmed removed

strengths: Clean 1:1 fix with no scope creep — only the flagged hardcoded values were changed
All 27 tests pass after the fix
Tests and CSS were updated in lockstep, no drift
CSS variable naming is consistent and semantic (var(--primary-color), var(--accent-orange), etc.)

issues.description: .btn:hover uses hardcoded #005a33 (darkened green) without a CSS variable. This is a hover-state shade variant, not a direct brand color reference. Acceptable pattern but could be improved with a --primary-color-dark variable for consistency.
.btn-danger:hover uses hardcoded #ff6666 (lightened red) without a CSS variable. Same pattern as above — hover shade variant. Could use --accent-red-light for consistency.

stage_2.assessment: The primary issue from Cycle 1 (hardcoded hex values in status badge and board-status styles) has been completely resolved. All 12 instances now correctly reference CSS variables. The two remaining hardcoded hex values are hover-state shade variants that were not in scope of the original finding and represent a common, acceptable CSS pattern. The rgba() transparency values in text-shadow and background are structural constants that cannot use CSS rgba() with variables. Overall this is a clean, complete fix.
